note_convention: All 'note' / 'midi' values use middle C = C4 = MIDI 60 and are the sounding pitch. Several sources name their files in another octave: VSCO 2 CE (except the solo violin) and most of VCSL (everything used here except the Steinway piano, pipe organ and concert harp) name middle C 'C3', so 12 was added; Black And Green Guitars and Growlybass name their notes an octave above the sounding pitch, as does Ganjo, and the legato vocal names its notes an octave above the sung pitch, so 12 was subtracted; Karoryfer x bigcat cello names middle C 'C3', so 12 was added. Every octave conversion was confirmed by measuring the pitch of the downloaded file. 'source_note' is the note token exactly as it appears in the source file name. 'measured_cents' (where present) is the measured pitch minus the stated pitch in cents; it is omitted where the measurement was not reliable.

instruments.name: Grand Piano
instruments.comment: Steinway B, close microphones, no sustain pedal, velocity layer 3 of 2-4. Top notes are stretch-tuned (G#7 about +24 cents).

instruments.name: Pianet Electric Piano
instruments.comment: Hohner Pianet T, FF layer, mono 16-bit FLAC; full natural decays. CC BY 3.0: attribution required (see sources).

instruments.name: Wurlitzer Electric Piano
instruments.comment: Wurlitzer EP200, 'f' layer, mono 16-bit FLAC. Short samples (1 to 5 s) that stop while still 12 to 25 dB below their peak: fade or loop them. Normalised to full scale by the author (1 to 3 full-scale samples in five files). CC BY 3.0: attribution required (see sources).

instruments.name: Pipe Organ
instruments.comment: Loud manual registration; 16-bit and quiet (peaks -16 to -29 dBFS): normalise. C3 and C6 have a strong octave partial.

instruments.name: Acoustic Guitar
instruments.comment: Archtop acoustic guitar recorded with a microphone (not a flat-top), velocity layer 3 of 4, mono.

instruments.name: Electric Guitar
instruments.comment: Green Gretsch Anniversary, direct signal, forte layer, mono; about 20 ms of lead-in.

instruments.name: Electric Bass
instruments.comment: Squier Jazz Bass, direct signal, forte layer, mono; every file is exactly 6 s and cut at about -50 to -65 dB.

instruments.name: Upright Bass
instruments.comment: 1958 double bass, pizzicato, velocity layer 3 of 4, mono. Sympathetic string resonance in every note; automatic pitch tracking is unreliable here, pitches were confirmed from the spectrum (all within about 21 cents).

instruments.name: Violin
instruments.comment: Solo violin, arco with vibrato, forte.

instruments.name: Viola
instruments.comment: Solo viola, arco, ff, anechoic chamber, no vibrato; AIFF files of 2.5 to 4.9 s with 0.1 to 0.5 s of leading silence. Licence is the University of Iowa's own unrestricted-use statement, not a formal licence.

instruments.name: Cello
instruments.comment: Solo cello, sustained, mf, mono. Files are cut for looping: they start and end at full level with no natural release.

instruments.name: String Ensemble
instruments.comment: Built from three VSCO 2 CE sections: cello section (C2 to A3), viola section (D4, A4), violin section (E5 to D6), sustained with vibrato, loudest layer. Mixed 16- and 24-bit.

instruments.name: Trumpet
instruments.comment: Sustained, loudest layer (v3).

instruments.name: Trombone
instruments.comment: Tenor trombone, sustained, loudest layer (v3); 16-bit and quiet (peaks -15 to -25 dBFS).

instruments.name: French Horn
instruments.comment: Sustained; layer v3 where it exists, otherwise v1 (A1, D5, F5); levels differ between notes (peaks -8 to -22 dBFS).

instruments.name: Tenor Saxophone
instruments.comment: Non-vibrato, layer vl3. A#5 is in the altissimo register.

instruments.name: Flute
instruments.comment: Sustained with vibrato (the non-vibrato set is much noisier on the low notes).

instruments.name: Clarinet
instruments.comment: Long sustains, loudest layer (v3); 16-bit, room noise about 40 to 55 dB below the note. The top note is relabelled (see file).

files.relabelled: source file name says F#5 (F#6 at C4 = 60) but the recording is an F6; relabelled to the measured pitch

instruments.name: Solo Voice Aah
instruments.comment: One deep male voice singing 'ah' (not a choir), D2 to G#3 only. The singer is flat on several notes (see measured_cents) and the files end at full level with no release. Most notes above A2 in the source are 30 to 55 cents flat and the two lowest are unsteady; those were left out.

instruments.name: Harp
instruments.comment: Concert harp, forte layer; 16-bit and quiet in the bass (peaks -20 to -30 dBFS). The whole harp is about 10 cents flat; the lowest (E1) and highest (F7) strings in the source are 30 cents or more flat and were left out.

instruments.name: Harpsichord
instruments.comment: French harpsichord, sustains; 48 kHz 24-bit.

instruments.name: Pizzicato Strings
instruments.comment: Built from VSCO 2 CE cello section (C2 to C4) and violin section (F#4 to D6) pizzicato; section pizzicati have a naturally blurred pitch. Mixed 16- and 24-bit.

instruments.name: Banjo
instruments.comment: Six-string guitar banjo. The source instrument is tuned 30 to 50 cents sharp; only takes measured within 30 cents were chosen, so the range is narrow (F#3 to B4) and the notes are short (0.7 to 1.8 s). 32-bit float WAV normalised to full scale.

instruments.name: Psaltery
instruments.comment: Bowed psaltery, plucked articulation.

instruments.name: Dan Tranh
instruments.comment: Vietnamese zither (koto-like), normal pluck, forte, mono.

instruments.name: Kalimba
instruments.comment: Kenyan kalimba in its own traditional tuning; only the tines within about 30 cents of equal temperament were chosen (B3 to D#5). Neighbouring tines ring in sympathy in every sample. D#5 is about +27 cents at the attack.

instruments.name: Marimba
instruments.comment: Loud layer; 24-bit but quiet (peaks -15 to -26 dBFS).

instruments.name: Vibraphone
instruments.comment: Soft mallets, layer v2; 16-bit. The lowest bar (F3) has a strong upper partial at the attack.

instruments.name: Glockenspiel
instruments.comment: Loud layer; 16-bit and quiet (peaks about -24 dBFS); 8 to 24 cents sharp.

instruments.name: Tubular Bells
instruments.comment: Orchestral chimes. The note is the strike tone (an octave below the fourth partial), confirmed from the partials, not by the automatic pitch tracker. Files end while still ringing at about -40 to -54 dB.

instruments.name: Acoustic Kit
instruments.comment: Kick, snare, hi-hats, high and mid tom, crash and ride are one jazz kit (Virtuosity Drums: kick from the kick microphone, snare and toms from the mid pair, cymbals from the overheads; FLAC 48 kHz 24-bit). tom_low is a concert tom and tambourine, shaker, clap, cowbell and woodblock are orchestral percussion from VCSL.

instruments.name: Orchestral Effects
instruments.comment: Acoustic stand-ins for impacts, risers and sweeps: gong, concert bass drum, clash cymbals, anvil, slapstick, suspended-cymbal crescendos, a bass-drum roll crescendo and wind chimes. No vinyl noise and no synthetic risers were found.

not_found.name: Choir
not_found.why: No multi-voice choir with a clear CC0 / CC BY licence was found on the listed sources. A single male solo voice ('Solo Voice Aah', D2 to G#3) is included as the nearest thing; a choir pad should be synthesised.

not_found.name: Rhodes electric piano
not_found.why: jRhodes3d (sfzinstruments/jlearman.jRhodes3d) licenses its samples CC BY-NC, which has a non-commercial clause, so it was not used. A Hohner Pianet T and a Wurlitzer EP200 (CC BY 3.0) are included instead.

not_found.name: Tonewheel / drawbar organ
not_found.why: Only pipe organs were found under a clean licence; a Hammond-style organ should be synthesised.

not_found.name: Flat-top steel-string or nylon acoustic guitar
not_found.why: The only cleanly licensed single-note acoustic guitar found is a microphone-recorded archtop (included as Acoustic Guitar). The University of Iowa guitar page offers multi-note scale files (its zip archives were not inspected); GitHub reports no licence file for OvationGuitar on sfzinstruments.

not_found.name: Five-string banjo
not_found.why: FlameStudios Kay 5-String Banjo is GPL-3.0, not a permissive sample licence, so it was not used. A six-string guitar banjo (CC0, narrow in-tune range) is included.

not_found.name: Mandolin, ukulele, koto, music box
not_found.why: GitHub reports no licence file for Terkelsen.Mandolin on sfzinstruments; no ukulele, koto or music box was found on the listed sources. Dan Tranh (a koto-like zither), psaltery, harpsichord, kalimba and pizzicato strings are included.

not_found.name: Vinyl noise
not_found.why: Not present in any of the checked sources; synthesise it.

not_found.name: Synthetic risers and cinematic impacts
not_found.why: Only acoustic ones exist in the checked sources (cymbal and bass-drum crescendos, gong, bass drum, anvil, slapstick), included under Orchestral Effects. Noise sweeps and sub drops should be synthesised.

not_found.name: Third drum-kit tom from the same kit
not_found.why: Virtuosity Drums has only a high and a low tom; the lowest tom in Acoustic Kit is a VCSL concert tom recorded in a different room.
